steps.say: Liver cancer is staged by tumour bulk, liver function and fitness together. Small tumours in a working liver are cured by removal or burning, while invasion of the main vein or spread beyond the liver moves treatment to drugs.
steps.tx: **Barcelona Clinic** (liver cancer staging) stage **0** and **A** disease with a single tumour of any size or 3 nodules under **3 cm** (three centimetres) for resection or ablation, while **portal vein tumour thrombus** (cancer in the main vein) marks **stage C** (advanced) needing systemic therapy.

steps.say: In a scarred liver, the scan pattern alone proves cancer and a needle is rarely needed. A bright blush in the arterial phase that fades in the venous phase is the hallmark, backed by a high blood marker.
steps.tx: **Alpha-fetoprotein** (liver cancer blood marker) over **400 ng per mL** (four hundred units) with **arterial hyperenhancement** (bright arterial blush) plus portal **washout** (venous fading) on multiphasic scans diagnoses HCC in cirrhosis without biopsy and avoids its needle bleeding risk entirely.

vis.alt: Two liver diagrams showing a bright arterial nodule that fades in the venous phase with vein invasion.
vis.caption: HCC imaging: arterial enhancement with portal washout in a cirrhotic liver, plus portal vein tumour thrombus. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Replacing the whole liver cures the tumour and the diseased organ together. Strict size limits pick patients whose cancer will not return, and most are alive years later.
steps.tx: **Milan** (transplant size rules) allows a single tumour up to **5 cm** (five centimetres) or 3 nodules up to **3 cm** (three centimetres) without **vascular invasion** (vessel penetration), selecting transplant candidates under the **Milan criteria** (size rules for grafting) with **4-year** (four year) survival over **70 percent** (seventy percent).

steps.say: Tiny tumours can be burned through a needle without any cut. The burn must cover the nodule plus a safety rim, and newer probes handle spots near big vessels better.
steps.tx: **Radiofrequency ablation** (needle heat destruction) cures tumours under **3 cm** (three centimetres) with **1 cm** (one centimetre) **ablative margin** (burned safety rim), while microwave ablation suits perivascular lesions because of less **heat-sink** (vessel cooling) effect from adjacent flowing blood nearby.

steps.say: Several nodules that cannot be cut or burned are starved instead. Oily chemotherapy is floated into the liver artery and the feeding branches are plugged, and the cycle repeats while scans show benefit.
steps.tx: Transarterial **chemoembolisation** (artery chemotherapy with plugging) with doxorubicin in oil suits intermediate multinodular disease without vascular invasion, repeated on demand by **mRECIST** (imaging response rules) on follow-up scans for as long as the liver tolerates treatment without failing or decompensating.

steps.say: Advanced disease is now treated with medicines that unmask the tumour to the immune system while starving its blood supply. Bleeding risk in swollen veins must be checked first with a camera.
steps.tx: **Atezolizumab** (immune checkpoint drug) with **bevacizumab** (vessel-starving drug) is first-line systemic therapy for advanced HCC with Child-Pugh **A** (preserved liver) function after variceal screening, beating sorafenib in the **IMBRAVE150** (landmark drug trial) on overall survival in advanced disease across the globe.

vis.alt: Outline of the liver and bile tree marking tumour sites with an inset of arterial uptake and venous washout.
vis.caption: Hepatobiliary tumour sites with arterial uptake and venous washout pattern guiding treatment choice. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A rare cancer of the young grows in a healthy liver and looks different under the microscope, with a scarred centre. Wide surgery removing nearby glands lets most live for years, with no diseased liver left behind.
steps.tx: **Fibrolamellar** (young noncirrhotic variant) HCC shows a **central scar** (fibrous core) with calcification, and aggressive resection with nodal clearance gives **5-year** (five year) survival near **70 percent** (seventy percent) without underlying liver disease in young operated patients followed long term.

steps.say: A tumour that bursts bleeds into the belly and the patient arrives pale and shocked. Blocking the artery first stops the bleeding, and the liver is removed weeks later once strength returns.
steps.tx: Ruptured HCC with **haemoperitoneum** (blood in the belly) needs transarterial embolisation first for haemostasis, then staged hepatectomy after **4 to 6 weeks** (four to six weeks) once the patient stabilises fully and the liver recovers enough for major surgery to proceed safely.
